newsitem.title: UK: Euro fuel oil markets sickly, traders hesitant.
newsitem.headline: Euro fuel oil markets sickly, traders hesitant.

text.p: European fuel markets were sickly on Wednesday as crude lost value and dealers hesitated to commit themselves to a position, traders said.
High sulphur fuel barges lost $1 to trade at $85, $84 and then $83 a tonne fob ARA, with continuing poor bunker demand mostly to blame.
Trade was extremely thin in the afternoon.
"It's been a rather stagnant, boring day," said one trader.
"I don't think crude has had much impact as fuel never rallied in the first place," said another. "It is more that there is clear oversupply on the prompt side because of the weak bunker demand."

Not even Singapore's renewed burst of health could drag the European market higher, though a high sulphur cargo deal, heard to be at $79 a tonne fob, from Britain to a trader with a short into Portugal boosted that sector.
Traders said the material was good quality and discounted its effect on the market.
Crude's 30-cent fall on the back of bearish U.S. stock data pressured one percent swaps, which dragged down notional physical numbers. Very little discussion was heard.
